## Motivation

The Diffusion contribution guide still requires the legacy `[diffusion] <scope>: <subject>` format, which conflicts with the repository-wide PR-title check.

## Changes

- Document the existing `[Type] [Hardware] scope: title` convention in the general contribution guide, with the hardware tag optional.
- Replace the Diffusion-specific convention with `diffusion` and `diffusion/<submodule-or-model>` scope examples, including `[Perf] diffusion/scheduler: Reduce scheduling overhead`.
- Distinguish PR titles from development commit messages and preserve the old `#commit-message-convention` anchor.

Documentation only; no runtime or CI behavior changes.

## Validation

- Pre-commit passed on both changed files.
- All seven distinct documented title examples passed the exact script used by the existing PR-title workflow.
- Verified the new cross-page link and preserved legacy anchor.
- Mintlify 4.2.559 `broken-links --check-anchors --check-redirects` passed with no broken links.
- Mintlify 4.2.559 `validate` passed.

@@ -104,6 +104,30 @@ GSM8K is too easy for many state-of-the-art models, so use a more challenging or
 ## Benchmark the speed
 Refer to [Benchmark and Profiling](./benchmark_and_profiling).
 
+## Pull request titles
+
+Use the repository-wide format checked by CI:
+
+```text
+[Type] scope: title
+[Type] [Hardware] scope: title
+```
+
+- **Type**: `Feat`, `Fix`, `Refactor`, `Perf`, `Doc`, `Test`, `CI`, or `Chore`.
+- **Scope**: A required module or model name. Use `/` for submodules, such as `diffusion/scheduler`; there is no fixed scope list or letter-case requirement.
+- **Hardware**: Optional, for hardware-specific changes only. Use a single uppercase tag, such as `AMD` or `NVIDIA`, except for the canonical spellings `Intel`, `Apple`, `Huawei`, and `Ascend`.
+- **Title**: A short, clear description in the imperative mood. Use one space between fields and after the colon, with no leading or trailing whitespace.
+
+For example:
+
+```text
+[Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing
+[Perf] diffusion/scheduler: Reduce scheduling overhead
+[Perf] [AMD] diffusion/attention: Optimize decode performance
+```
+
+For reverts, keep GitHub's default `Revert "original title"` format. The PR-title check validates PR titles, not individual development commit messages.
+
 ## Requesting a review for merge
 You can follow the pull request merge process described in [MAINTAINER.md](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md).
 You will need to work with the Merge Oncall, Codeowner, and other reviewers to get their approvals.

@@ -21,24 +21,21 @@ Vibe-coded PRs are welcome — we judge code quality, not how it was produced. T
 - **No over-catching.** Don't guard against errors that virtually never happen in practice.
 - **Test before submitting.** AI-generated code can be subtly wrong — verify correctness end-to-end.
 
-## Commit Message Convention
+<a id="commit-message-convention" />
 
-We follow a structured commit message format to maintain a clean history.
+## Pull request titles
+
+Follow the repository-wide [PR title convention](/docs/developer_guide/contribution_guide#pull-request-titles). Use `diffusion` as the scope, or `diffusion/<submodule-or-model>` when a more specific scope helps.
 
-**Format:**
 ```text
-[diffusion] <scope>: <subject>
+[Perf] diffusion/scheduler: Reduce scheduling overhead
+[Fix] diffusion/cli: Fix argument parsing
+[Feat] diffusion/wan: Add model support
+[Doc] diffusion: Update the contribution guide
+[Perf] [NVIDIA] diffusion/attention: Optimize attention kernels
 ```
 
-**Examples:**
-- `[diffusion] cli: add --perf-dump-path argument`
-- `[diffusion] scheduler: fix deadlock in batch processing`
-- `[diffusion] model: support Stable Diffusion 3.5`
-
-**Rules:**
-- **Prefix**: Always start with `[diffusion]`.
-- **Scope** (Optional): `cli`, `scheduler`, `model`, `pipeline`, `docs`, etc.
-- **Subject**: Imperative mood, short and clear (e.g., "add feature" not "added feature").
+Put the change type in the first bracketed tag. `diffusion` belongs in the scope, not in a hardware tag or a separate `[Diffusion]` prefix. Omit the hardware tag unless the change is hardware-specific.
